https://tribune.com.pk/story/2620278/mil.text: Home Sindh Millers seek direct wheat imports PFMA argues open-market mechanism would ensure cheaper flour for consumers while reducing risk of corruption With Pakistan facing a wheat shortfall, the Pakistan Flour Mills Association (PFMA) has urged the federal government to allow flour mills to directly import wheat, saying the move would ensure cheaper flour for consumers, promote competition and avoid corruption risks linked to state-run imports. PFMA argued that an open-market mechanism would ensure cheaper flour for consumers while reducing the risk of corruption. Speaking to The Express Tribune , PFMA Sindh Chairman Abdul Junaid Aziz said the federal government had decided to initially import one million tonnes of wheat through the Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP). However, he argued that imports and distribution through the TCP, coupled with subsidies, could increase the risk of corruption. To address these concerns and promote healthy competition, he urged the government to immediately permit flour mills to import wheat directly under a deregulated, open-market mechanism. Aziz said the association had warned the government and relevant institutions two months ago that domestic wheat production was expected to fall, but the warning went unheeded. Had policymakers acted at the time, he said, Pakistan could have imported cheaper wheat from Russia and Ukraine during the ceasefire period via the Strait of Hormuz. Instead, the country would now have to rely on costlier imports from Australia, Romania and Canada. He estimated that Pakistan would need to import between three million and 3.5 million tonnes of wheat to meet domestic demand. https://bnonews.com/index.php/2026/08/na.text: Credit: NATO Advertisment17 Share Tweet A drone believed to be Russian was shot down by a Spanish F-18 fighter jet after entering Romanian airspace near the border with Moldova, according to Romanian and NATO officials. The incident happened at 4:44 a.m. on Sunday when Romania’s surveillance systems detected an aerial target entering the country from Moldova, about 24 kilometers (15 miles) north of Galati. A Spanish F-18 which was carrying out an air policing mission established radar contact with the drone. The fighter jet was given permission to engage the target and shot it down at 5:01 a.m., according to Romania’s Ministry of National Defence. A possible impact site was identified between the communities of Baleni and Cudalbi in Galati County, in an unpopulated area. Aerial and ground searches were carried out in the area, where authorities found fragments from the drone and from the interceptor missile. The missile fragments were safely neutralized by an explosive ordnance disposal team, while drone debris was collected for forensic examination. Article continues below the player “Additional details regarding Sunday’s incident remain under investigation, but the drone appears to be Russian,” said U.S. Army Colonel Martin O’Donnell, a spokesperson for NATO’s military headquarters. NATO said two Spanish F-18s were scrambled during the incident. The fighter jets are part of a Spanish deployment at Mihail Kogalniceanu Air Base, where Spain has stationed seven F-18s and about 200 personnel. https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/nearly-.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.08.24 19:05 Nearly half of Lithuanians pleased with the change of prime minister – poll Translated by Karolis Broga Source: Elta EN Nearly half of Lithuanians pleased with the change of prime minister – poll PHOTO: Orestas Gurevičius | Elta Follow Delfi on Google Nearly half of Lithuanians view the Social Democratic Party’s (LSDP) decision to replace Prime Minister Inga Ruginienė with Mindaugas Sinkevičius favourably, according to a poll commissioned by the public broadcaster LRT. It has transpired that 47% of respondents have a positive opinion about the change of the prime minister. Of them, 11% have a very positive and 36% a rather positive opinion. Meanwhile, 30% of respondents have a negative opinion about the move, whereas a quarter did not have an opinion on the matter or did not answer the question.The most positive opinion about the change of the prime minister was among Social Democratic voters, as 71% of them agree with the move. Whereas the most negative opinion about the change was among supporters of the Nemunas Dawn party, 42% of whom disapprove of the move. Supporters of other parties more often had a favourable rather than an unfavourable view about the change of the prime minister. The poll was carried out by the joint Lithuanian and British market and public opinion research company Baltijos tyrimai on 21–31 July 2026. 1,002 Lithuanian citizens aged 18 and over were personally interviewed across 108 polling locations. The margin of error is 3.1%. As reported, after a reshuffle of the ruling coalition, the new Cabinet of Ministers took oath in mid-July. Former Prime Minister Inga Ruginienė returned to her previous position of Minister of Social Security and Labour, whereas Jonava District Mayor Mindaugas Sinkevičius was appointed as Prime Minister. https://www.politico.eu/article/poland-p.text: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a ‘direct threat’ was averted at a border crossing with Ukraine on Wednesday night and warned of further incidents linked to Russia in the near future. His comments came just one day after a Russian drone hit a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova, killing two people and wounding several others. “Last night, thanks to cooperation between our services and their Ukrainian counterparts, a direct threat to a border crossing was averted,” Tusk said in a press conference after a meeting of the Visegrád Group leaders in Bratislava Thursday. Advertisement Advertisement Tusk did not provide any further details about the nature of the threat or which of the 18 border crossings between Poland and Ukraine was affected. The prime minister added that the incident was just a taste of what is to come and noted he had received a “fairly precise report” from the CIA regarding possible events in the coming months. “We must anticipate various scenarios; both Poland and all of Europe need to ⁠be ​prepared for different possibilities concerning the ​situation not only on the Russian-Ukrainian front but also along the EU’s eastern ​flank.” The incident at the border crossing between Moldova and Ukraine’s Odesa region left two people dead, causing President Maia Sandu to call for further European air defense support for Ukraine. Russia also struck a Moldova-Ukraine border crossing in August . “As you know, Russia has already resorted to provocative attacks on border crossings—for instance, in Moldova. We expect similar actions targeting border crossings with Ukraine in other countries, including Poland,” said Tusk. Advertisement Advertisement In August, after a briefing with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, he warned that “escalation from Russia’s side is progressing,” and called for more air support for Ukraine as it is “crucial for our security.” He said the next six months would be decisive and made it clear that provocations against NATO members should not be ruled out. The CIA did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Jalen Beckford contributed to this report.

https://www.dw.com/en/north-and-south-ko.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NaaE North Korea has been fortifying the border after a shift in policy against Seoul, calling it a 'foe' [FILE: June 2019] Image: Ahn Young-joon/AP/picture alliance Advertisement Pyongyang and Seoul are trading increasingly hostile accusations across the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) that divides the peninsula, 10 days after three South Korean soldiers were injured by a land mine on the South's side of the border. The latest tensions may reflect a broader North Korean effort to test South Korea 's resolve while extending its control to the outer limits of its territory, including an area that has effectively been a no-man's land for more than 70 years, according to a professor of foreign policy at South Korea's Kyung Hee University. "The North revised its constitution in March this year and officially stated that they intend to define the absolute geographical limits of the nation, and that includes within the DMZ," said Choo. "They want to maximize their territory and it is my sense that they would like to push the Military Demarcation Line [MDL] — the half-way point in the DMZ — further south," he told DW. "I see the placing of landmines on the South's side of the line as a purely political act by the North, an attempt to threaten and intimidate the South." Why Seoul blames North Korea The three men were part of an 18-strong patrol clearing a new route through the DMZ as part of an investigation into the activities of North Korean troops in the western sector of the zone. The four-kilometer-wide strip of land has divided the peninsula since the Korean War ended in an armistice in 1953. The DMZ is a fortified buffer zone between the two Koreas that has been in place since 1953 Image: Soeren Stache/dpa/picture alliance Shortly before 11 a.m. on September 21, the patrol was around 10 meters south of the MDL when a staff sergeant detonated a mine. A second mine went off as the unit commander approached to provide assistance. Both men were successfully evacuated and have undergone surgery, with a third soldier treated for minor wounds. The South Korean military has conducted an investigation with the United Nations Command, which administers the armistice on the border, and concluded in a report released this week that the mine was of North Korean origin. The Joint Chiefs of Staff on Wednesday accused the North of sowing mines to the south of the MDL, a breach of the armistice agreement, and demanded an apology from Pyongyang and a commitment to halt the construction of further fortifications along the border. "This constitutes a blatant violation of the Armistice Agreement and undermines the spirit of existing inter-Korean agreements and must be halted immediately," Kang Hyun-woo, chief director of operations, said in a press briefing. "North Korea must immediately cease activities that heighten tensions on the Korean Peninsula, such as its so-called 'border fortification.' We strongly demand an apology and responsible measures from the North," Kang added. In a statement, the UN Command said it had "determined that an Armistice Agreement violation occurred. UNC is addressing the violation through established Armistice mechanisms." Prisoner swap: From North to South Korea via Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Many in the South are demanding more resolute action on the grounds that failure to respond will be taken as a sign of weakness in Seoul. Na Kyung-won, a politician from the conservative opposition People Power Party (PPP), has demanded that the South Korean military carry out exercises simulating a "decapitation attack" against North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. She has also called for the restart of propaganda broadcasts from loudspeakers on the border and for dissident groups to be allowed to launch balloons carrying propaganda into the North. A pattern of border confrontations Yu Yong-weon, also of the PPP, told reporters on Wednesday that North Korean troops had crossed the MDL around 20 times in August and on 30 occasions in September. On each occasion, South Korean troops fired warning shots when the incursions were detected. An editorial in the Korea JoongAng Daily on Thursday said North Korea must be "held accountable" for the incident, arguing that Pyongyang's denial of responsibility "demands a firm response, clear accountability and stronger border enforcement." Kim Jong Un's sister Kim Yo Jong has accused Seoul of conspiracy after it blamed Pyongyang for the blast in the DMZ Image: Yuri Smityuk/TASS/dpa/picture alliance The North is not backing down, however, with Kim Yo Jong , sister of leader Kim Jong Un, accusing the South of staging a provocation and threatening to retaliate. In a statement published by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) on Wednesday, Kim Yo Jong dismissed the South's allegations as a "self-staged farce" and accused the "South Korean armed gangs" of using the incident to justify political and military provocations against Pyongyang. Accident or calculated provocation? Andrei Lankov, a professor of history and international relations at Seoul's Kookmin University, is more willing to view the landmine detonations as an accident. "It makes no sense to me for North Korea to do this deliberately," he said. "At the moment, the North wants to keep a low profile and do nothing that could provoke the South. There is no gain in a deliberate attack like this." Lankov believes a more likely scenario is that the mines were shifted from the northern side of the MDL in heavy rain or natural movements of the terrain, meaning that the North's protestations of innocence are genuine. "I also do not think the South Korean government has any interest in escalating the situation further and that they will hope this is quickly forgotten," he said. "They will want to brush it under the carpet." Choo, however, is less convinced and senses a growing anger in South Korean society that the government is not standing up to provocations from north of the border. "I believe that resuming the propaganda broadcasts over the border would be an effective response, but I do not believe this government will do that," he said. "This government is trying very hard to connect with the North, but I see a failure to take a firm line this time being interpreted in the North as a sign of weakness in Seoul. "Not responding would give Pyongyang a green light to push a little more and then a little more again," he said. "There is a lot of anger here that the government is not doing enough to protect soldiers who are serving on the DMZ, to protect the people and to protect our territory." https://www.dw.com/en/nvidia-shareholder.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PH9N Prefer DW on Google Huang led Nvidia's transformation from a gaming chipmaker into a central supplier of AI technology (FILE: 21/10/2026) Image: Soeren Stache/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Shareholders sued chipmaker Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, on Monday, accusing them of concealing his alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset . The proposed class action adds to investigations into whether Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence, raising questions about the security of sensitive information at the world's most valuable chipmaker. What does the lawsuit allege? The complaint, filed in federal court in San Jose, California, alleges that Nvidia and Huang misled investors about his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who is not related to him. Shareholders say the defendants failed to disclose national security concerns that threatened Nvidia's reputation and business prospects. They are seeking unspecified damages. The New York Times reported last month on the alleged relationship and said US authorities had concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset. What have Nvidia and Huang said? Nvidia announced an independent investigation Sunday into reports that Huang had been the "target of a foreign intelligence effort." Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in an open letter, but did not identify the woman. Nvidia investigates CEO after reports of affair with Chinese spy To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully," he said. "I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security." Nvidia shares closed down 4.3% Monday. The lawsuit was filed five minutes after US markets closed. How have Washington and Beijing responded? US President Donald Trump said Monday that the FBI was investigating the matter, while expressing support for Huang. Trump said he had spoken to the executive earlier that day. "He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy," Trump told reporters. China denied conducting an intelligence operation targeting Huang. "The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. Why does the case matter for the AI industry? Huang co-founded Nvidia and led its transformation from a maker of gaming chips into a leading supplier of the computing technology powering artificial intelligence . Its advanced chips have become a focus of US-China competition, with Washington restricting exports to limit Beijing's access to the technology. Huang has pushed for looser restrictions on sales to China. The investigations have intensified scrutiny of his leadership and whether confidential company information was compromised.
